title: Etale horizontal compact-support exchange is the composition mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. All schemes below are Noetherian, meaning they admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. In a Cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{u'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow u&Y,\end{array}$$
assume that $f,f',u,u'$ are separated finite-type morphisms, $u,u'$ are etale, and give these morphisms and their equal composites $fu'=uf'$ compactifications [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $F_a=Ra_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})$ for $a=u,u'$, with the sum/evaluation adjunction $S_a\dashv a^*$ and counit $\epsilon_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Let $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ be the canonical proper-support comparison of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], followed by its identification of proper-support sections with the sum extension. Use the specified proper/open composition maps and compact-support exchange $C_{f,u}:u^*F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}u'^*$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Define
$$\delta=(d_uF_{f'})\circ\alpha_{u,f'}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{f,u'}\circ F_f(d_{u'}^{-1}):F_fS_{u'}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_uF_{f'}.$$
For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the following equality holds:
$$F_f(\epsilon_{u',M})\circ\delta_{u'^*M}^{-1}=\epsilon_{u,F_fM}\circ S_u(C_{f,u,M}^{-1}):S_uF_{f'}u'^*M\longrightarrow F_fM.$$
Equivalently, the left side has adjunct $C_{f,u,M}^{-1}$ under $S_u\dashv u^*$. This equality uses the specified compactification exchange, not an arbitrary natural isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: Tags 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition) and 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), with etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) and Tag 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale). Agent-stated etale-horizontal extension of the proper/open tower mate calculation, serving ancestor proof Step 1: compatibility of smooth-base-change/co-projection factors with composition.

proof.text:
Use the specified comparisons of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] throughout; juxtaposition of maps below composes right to left. Transport the adjunctions of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] across $d_a$, writing $\eta^c_a=a^*(d_a^{-1})\eta^S_a$ and $\epsilon^c_a=\epsilon^S_a d_a$ for $F_a\dashv a^*$, $a=u,u'$. For $L=u'^*M$ and $N=F_{f'}L$, put
$$\kappa_M=F_f(\epsilon^c_{u',M})\alpha_{f,u'}^{-1}\alpha_{u,f'}:F_uN\longrightarrow F_fM.$$
Taking inverses in the definition in the statement gives the typed formula
$$\delta_L^{-1}=F_f(d_{u',L})\circ\alpha_{f,u'}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{u,f'}\circ d_{u,N}^{-1}.$$
Thus the left side of the item is $\kappa_Md_{u,N}^{-1}$. We will prove $C_{f,u,M}u^*(\kappa_M)\eta^c_{u,N}=1_N$; invertibility of $C$ then identifies the adjunct of this map as required.

source.place: Tags 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek); formal transport of an adjunction

proof.text: Form $V=Y'\times_Y Y'$ with projections $p_1,p_2$, and $P=X'\times_Y Y'$ with projections $a:P\to X'$ (the old copy) and $b:P\to Y'$ (the new base). Write $h=(f'a,b):P\to V$ and $v=(u'a,b):P\to X'$ (the new copy). Then $p_2h=b=f'v$ and the squares $(h,f';p_1,a)$ and $(v,u';u',a)$ are Cartesian. The diagonals $t:Y'\to V$ and $e:X'\to P$ satisfy $p_it=1$, $ae=ve=1$, $he=tf'$, and the square with vertical edges $h,f'$ and horizontal edges $e,t$ is Cartesian. These are identities of fibre products. The projections of $V$ and the maps $a,v$ are separated etale finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits, lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. The section theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] applied to $p_2$ and $v$ makes $t,e$ clopen immersions. The same finite-type base-change theorem applies to $h,b$. The schemes $V,P$ are quasi-compact over $Y',X'$ and locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], hence have finite Noetherian affine covers. Each of $p_1,p_2,a,v,h,b$ is a base change of one of $u,u',f'$ or $fu'=uf'$, so pulling back the given compactification gives a compactification of it: the pulled-back open immersion is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and the pulled-back proper map is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The clopen immersions $t,e$ have the compactifications $(t,\mathrm{id})$, $(e,\mathrm{id})$. Thus every square used below is in the unbounded comparison theorem's scope.

Identify $F_t,F_e$ with termwise open extension using the open compactifications, as in [lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint]. Write $\epsilon_t,\epsilon_e$ for their evaluation counits. For a complex $B$ on $Y'$ and a complex $H$ on $X'$, define the diagonal insertions
$$J_B=F_{p_2}(\epsilon_{t,p_1^*B})\alpha_{p_2,t,B}^{-1}:B\longrightarrow F_{p_2}p_1^*B,$$
$$J'_H=F_v(\epsilon_{e,a^*H})\alpha_{v,e,H}^{-1}:H\longrightarrow F_va^*H.$$
Here $t^*p_1^*B=B$, $e^*a^*H=H$, $F_{p_2t}=F_1=1$ and $F_{ve}=1$ are the canonical identity comparisons. By the composition normalization in [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], after replacing the etale $F$'s by sum extension these are precisely the inclusions of the summands supported on the diagonal lifts: the open counit includes the diagonal component and is zero on the complement. This describes sheaf maps induced on the presheaf lift summands, not an objectwise description of sheaf sections.

source.place: Tags 0F7J, 0GKM; diagonal summands and the open evaluation counit

proof.text:
The base-change identity (1) of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility], applied to $u$ along itself and to $u'$ along itself, identifies $C_{u,u}$ and $C_{u',u'}$ with the specified sum-extension base-change maps after applying $d$. In the presheaf definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], the adjunction unit sends a section over an etale object of the source to the summand indexed by its structural lift. Under this self-base-change identification that lift is the diagonal lift; restriction of a lift and its value commutes with this description. Sheafification therefore gives the equalities
$$C_{u,u,B}\eta^c_{u,B}=J_B,\qquad C_{u',u',H}\eta^c_{u',H}=J'_H.$$
The composition normalization of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] used in Step 3 ensures that these use the specified $\alpha_{p_2,t}$ and $\alpha_{v,e}$, rather than arbitrary identifications of $F_{p_2t}$ and $F_{ve}$. All the functors in this check are exact sum extension or exact restriction, with the termwise adjunction of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]; the same equalities of chain maps give the identities for every unbounded complex.

Apply the already established open-horizontal mate theorem [lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint] to $h:P\to V$, the open $t:Y'\hookrightarrow V$, and its pullback $e:X'\hookrightarrow P$, with input $a^*L$. It gives the specific equality
$$F_h(\epsilon_{e,a^*L})\alpha_{h,e}^{-1}\alpha_{t,f'}
=\epsilon_{t,F_ha^*L}F_t(C_{h,t,a^*L}^{-1}):F_tF_{f'}L\longrightarrow F_ha^*L.\tag{O}$$
In particular this is the proper/open tower calculation already available for an open horizontal arrow, applied to the diagonal square, not the etale-horizontal assertion being proved. Its hypotheses hold by Step 2, and its compact-support and open-extension normalizations are exactly those used here.

source.place: Tags 0F7J and 0F7L; open-horizontal mate applied to the clopen diagonal

proof.text:
Put $Q=C_{f',p_1,L}:p_1^*N\to F_ha^*L$. Composite-base-change compatibility and identity normalization in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], since $p_1t=1$, give
$$C_{h,t,a^*L}\,t^*Q=1_N,\quad\text{so }t^*Q=C_{h,t,a^*L}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of the open counit and (O) now give the following calculation, whose source is $N$ and target is $F_{p_2}F_ha^*L$:
$$\begin{aligned}
F_{p_2}(Q)J_N
&=F_{p_2}(\epsilon_{t,F_ha^*L})F_{p_2}F_t(t^*Q)\alpha_{p_2,t,N}^{-1}\\
&=F_{p_2}(F_h(\epsilon_{e,a^*L}))F_{p_2}(\alpha_{h,e}^{-1})F_{p_2}(\alpha_{t,f'})\alpha_{p_2,t,N}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first line is just naturality of $\epsilon_t$ in the definition of $J$; the second substitutes the displayed value of $t^*Q$ into (O).

source.place: Tags 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek); naturality and the open mate equation

proof.text:
Postcompose Step 6 by $\alpha_{p_2,h,a^*L}$. Its naturality moves $F_{p_2}F_h(\epsilon_e)$ to $F_b(\epsilon_e)$. Associativity of $\alpha$ in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], applied to the triples $(p_2,h,e)$ and $(p_2,t,f')$, gives
$$\alpha_{p_2,h,F_eL}\,F_{p_2}(\alpha_{h,e}^{-1})F_{p_2}(\alpha_{t,f'})\alpha_{p_2,t,F_{f'}L}^{-1}=\alpha_{b,e,L}^{-1},$$
because $he=tf'$ and $p_2t=1$. Thus the resulting composite is
$$F_b(\epsilon_{e,a^*L})\alpha_{b,e,L}^{-1}.$$
On the other hand the definition of $J'_L$ and associativity for $(f',v,e)$, with $ve=1$ and $f'v=b$, identify this same map with $\alpha_{f',v,a^*L}F_{f'}(J'_L)$. We have therefore obtained the typed diagonal-insertion identity
$$\alpha_{p_2,h,a^*L}F_{p_2}(Q)J_N=\alpha_{f',v,a^*L}F_{f'}(J'_L).\tag{D}$$
This is a substitution into the stated associativity equations, not an additional geometric comparison lemma.

Write $w=uf'=fu'$ and $T=C_{w,u,L}:u^*F_wL\to F_ba^*L$. Compatibility of base change with composition in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], for the two factorizations of $w$, reads
$$T\,u^*(\alpha_{u,f',L})=\alpha_{p_2,h,a^*L}\,F_{p_2}(Q)\,C_{u,u,N},\tag{B1}$$
$$T\,u^*(\alpha_{f,u',L})=\alpha_{f',v,a^*L}\,F_{f'}(C_{u',u',L})\,C_{f,u,F_{u'}L}.\tag{B2}$$
These instantiate the same comparison theorem, respectively in the Cartesian squares $(h,f';p_1,a)$ and $(v,u';u',a)$ from Step 2. Naturality of its exchange also gives
$$C_{f,u,M}\,u^*F_f(\epsilon^c_{u',M})
=F_{f'}(u'^*\epsilon^c_{u',M})\,C_{f,u,F_{u'}L}.\tag{B3}$$
All three equations concern the specified proper/open-normalized maps. The first two have common target $F_ba^*L$; the last has target $N$.

source.place: Tags 0F7J and 0F7L; base change of each composition comparison and naturality

proof.text:
Substitute (B2) into (B3), then (B1) and Step 4 into the definition of $\kappa$. With $R=C_{u',u',L}$ this gives
$$\begin{aligned}
C_{f,u,M}u^*(\kappa_M)\eta^c_{u,N}
&=F_{f'}(u'^*\epsilon^c_{u',M})F_{f'}(R^{-1})\alpha_{f',v,a^*L}^{-1}\alpha_{p_2,h,a^*L}F_{p_2}(Q)J_N\\
&=F_{f'}\bigl((u'^*\epsilon^c_{u',M})R^{-1}J'_L\bigr)\\
&=F_{f'}\bigl((u'^*\epsilon^c_{u',M})\eta^c_{u',L}\bigr)=1_N.
\end{aligned}$$
The second line is (D), and the third is Step 4 for $u'$. The last equality is the triangle identity for the transported adjunction $F_{u'}\dashv u'^*$, since $L=u'^*M$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Each cancellation involves inverse comparison maps with the same source and target; no faithfulness of stalks or of degreewise evaluation on derived morphisms is used.

source.place: Tags 0F7J and 0F7L; substitution of the preceding equations and an adjunction triangle identity

proof.text:
Since $C_{f,u,M}$ is invertible [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], Step 9 says $u^*(\kappa_M)\eta^c_{u,N}=C_{f,u,M}^{-1}$. By the transported-unit formula from Step 1,
$$u^*(\kappa_Md_{u,N}^{-1})\eta^S_{u,N}=u^*(\kappa_M)\eta^c_{u,N}=C_{f,u,M}^{-1}.$$
The adjunction bijection of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] therefore gives
$$\kappa_Md_{u,N}^{-1}=\epsilon^S_{u,F_fM}S_u(C_{f,u,M}^{-1}).$$
Step 1 identified the left side with $F_f(\epsilon_{u',M})\delta_L^{-1}$, proving the asserted equality for every unbounded $M$. Nothing restricts the input to bounded or constructible complexes.
